summary: Four attacks, three clean and one low-severity finding on how the owners table records its reassignments. All 37 links resolve at both endpoints; all 7 owner stages and every 'formerly' stage resolve; the proposed Part II title obeys PROTOCOL section 15, reproducing the anchor's title exactly and adding ', Part II' before the subtitle — and it is a genuine improvement, since the atlas currently titles the roadmap 'Reductive groups, Part II: ...' while the anchor is 'Reductive algebraic groups'. On duplication, no other roadmap in either roadmap directory owns the parahoric, Bruhat-Tits, building or Iwahori material that RG2.2 and RG2.3 retain, so that content is uniquely held; the one real duplication in the family, the Deligne torus shared with ShimuraData D1, was already caught by the independent review and is handled in the owners table. The finding is that the 'formerly' field carries two different meanings, which a consumer computing what each layer lost would read wrongly.
checked: All 37 links, both endpoints, against every stage id in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ and research/blueprint/roadmaps/ (2040 stage ids indexed, in both the bare and the fully qualified form). No source and no target is missing.
All 7 owner entries: every 'owner' stage resolves, and every stage named in a 'formerly' list resolves.

The section-15 title rule. The anchor tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups is titled 'Reductive algebraic groups'; RS-31 proposes 'Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models', which reproduces the anchor's title exactly and appends ', Part II' before the colon. The proposal's declared 'extends' is the anchor. Note that this is a correction, not merely conformance: the atlas record for ReductiveGroupsPartII is currently titled 'Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arith...', which does not reproduce the anchor's title.

Duplication, against both roadmap directories, by screening every roadmap whose title or summary mentions parahoric, Bruhat-Tits, building, Iwahori, affine Weyl, valued root or apartment vocabulary. The only substantive hit is ReductiveGroupsPartII itself; the others (OptimalTransport, GeometricTopology, DenseGraphLimits, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory) match only on the ordinary word 'building'. So the apartment, building and Bruhat-Tits model content that RG2.2 and RG2.3 retain is not owned anywhere else.

The one duplication the family does contain was already found before me: the literal Deligne-torus construction shared between ShimuraData D1 and RG2.0a. RS-31 narrows D1 and assigns the construction to RG2.0a, and the independent review records that it 'Corrected the missed Deligne-torus duplication with ShimuraData D1 and preserved its Hodge work and D2 handoff'. I confirmed the owners table carries that assignment.

Consistency between each layer's 'action' and the owners table, which is where the finding comes from. Four layers are marked 'narrow' (RG2.1, RG2.4, RG2.5, ShimuraData:D1) and each loses one or two targets to another owner, which is coherent. Two layers marked 'keep' (RG2.0, RG2.3) also appear in a 'formerly' list. Reading their reasons shows they are correctly 'keep': RG2.0 says to 'Use the upstream functor-of-points/group-scheme dictionary ... the new topology/comparison is not supplied by that algebraic equivalence', and RG2.3 says to 'Use anchor group-scheme, quotient, unipotent-radical and reductivity notions: a supplied predicate is not a construction or proof of reductivity of this particular quotient'. Neither ever claimed the notion the owners table assigns elsewhere.

A false alarm of my own, recorded so it is not repeated: my first section-15 check compared the text before the colon against the anchor title directly and reported a failure. The rule is anchor title plus ', Part II', so the test must strip that suffix. The title is correct.

findings.where: research/blueprint/restructure/RS-31.result.json, the owners entries whose formerly lists are ["ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0"] and ["ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3"]
findings.claim: The 'formerly' field carries two different meanings in one table. For four layers it means 'this content moved out of that layer, which is therefore narrowed' (RG2.1, RG2.4, RG2.5 and ShimuraData:D1, all marked action 'narrow'). For two it means 'that layer uses this notion, which lives here' (RG2.0 and RG2.3, both correctly marked action 'keep'). A consumer computing what each layer lost from owners[].formerly would conclude that RG2.0 and RG2.3 are narrowed, contradicting their own action field, and would carry away content those layers retain. The proposal's substance is right in both cases and no layer is mis-scoped; only the encoding is ambiguous.
findings.evidence: The four genuine reassignments are distinguishable in the data, but not by 'formerly': the narrowed layers also carry 'suppliedBy' and 'keeps' fields (RG2.1 has suppliedBy ['tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups#layer-7-structure-theory'] and a 'keeps' note), while RG2.0 and RG2.3 carry neither. The two layers' own reasons make their status explicit. RG2.0 (action 'keep'): 'Retain all point-topology constructions, chart-independence, functoriality, separated finite-type local compactness/Hausdorffness, group continuity, integral compactness and congruence-neighbourhood results. Use the upstream functor-of-points/group-scheme dictionary and specialize the pinned GeneralLinear points equivalence for the GL_n acceptance test; the new topology/comparison is not supplied by that algebraic equivalence.' RG2.3 (action 'keep'): 'Retain construction of the connected smooth affine Bruhat-Tits O_E-model, root charts, generic fiber and integral-point characterization ... Use anchor group-scheme, quotient, unipotent-radical and reductivity notions: a supplied predicate is not a construction or proof of reductivity of this particular quotient.' The owner entries themselves state only a target and a formerly list, with no field marking them as reuse rather than reassignment: 'Group-scheme/functor-of-points dictionary used before local topologization' -> ReductiveGroups#layer-0-the-functor-of-points-and-the-three-way-dictionary, formerly RG2.0; and 'Reductivity over a field (smooth, connected, with trivial geometric unipotent radical), used on a special-fiber quotient' -> ReductiveGroups#layer-6-reductive-and-semisimple-groups, formerly RG2.3.
findings.fix: Distinguish the two relations in the owners table, leaving every layer action and every owner assignment as it stands. Either replace 'formerly' with 'usedBy' on the RG2.0 and RG2.3 entries (reading: this notion is used by that layer and owned here), or add a 'relation' field taking 'moved-from' and 'used-by' so that both cases are explicit. Both target strings already say 'used before local topologization' and 'used on a special-fiber quotient', so the intent is recoverable from the prose; the fix is to put it in a field a consumer can read.
